note: The check the operator believed was wired and was not. 916fe1a built the if/then -- 'stand-up is an if/then that asks, not acts' -- but applied it only to the committed dogfood decision store, which ships in the repo and is therefore always present, so its ask branch could never fire. Nothing asked whether a *Nestor* was stood up. nestor.home_init.ensure_home_layout, the scaffolder that would answer it, had zero callers: documented at README.md:338, announced at CHANGELOG.md:42, covered by tests/test_home_scaffold.py, wired to nothing. Adds a [nestor] section: present means one line and no prompt, absent means the agent is handed the question to put to the user.

decisions.question: Does the boot stand a Nestor up when it finds none, or ask?
decisions.commitment: It asks, and builds nothing on either branch. Present: one line naming the path and its counts, no prompt -- there is no choice to put to the user when the thing already exists. Absent: an _ask_prompt telling the agent to ask the user before proposing, naming the fix (`nestor demo`, or `python -m nestor.home_init` for a household seat). _stand_up_prompt was generalised into _ask_prompt so the brain's wording stays byte-identical while the tag, the reason it matters and the fix belong to each caller.
decisions.why: It is what was asked for, and it is the posture the repo already keeps: propose before acting, and a boot hook that quietly builds state is the failure it would be diagnosing. A prompt that borrowed the brain's rationale ('boots blind to what has already been decided') would be the boot lying about which question it asked -- a missing Nestor and a missing decision store are different facts with different fixes.

decisions.question: What counts as 'a Nestor is stood up', and where is that path resolved?
decisions.commitment: Two seats, one question. With $HOMESTEAD_HOME set it is a household host: stood up when home_init's layout.json marker is present -- the directory alone does not count, because hooks/review_receipt already creates paths under that same root without any layout having been laid out. Otherwise it is this product tree: stood up when the store the CLI opens by default exists, and that path is read off nestor.cli.build_parser().get_default('db') rather than restated in the hook.
decisions.why: nestor/homestead_paths.py is explicit that the household layout is not this tree's dev default, so a single probe would be wrong in one seat or the other. Reading the path off the CLI's own parser is the same rule _venv_python already keeps for the interpreter: a check that probed a different store from the one the agent's next command opens would report on a store nobody uses -- and that exact class of divergence is what let the detect-secrets gap survive (0124).

decisions.question: Why must the probe create nothing, and was that shown?
decisions.commitment: Because `nestor stats` on a tree with no store does not report 'no Nestor' -- it creates data/nestor.db and prints `0 pair(s)`. An absent Nestor and an empty one are indistinguishable the moment anything runs, so boot is the only honest moment to ask, and a probe that touched the path would destroy the answer and then report it. Shown: test_the_nestor_check_stands_nothing_up snapshots the tree before and after and requires it unchanged; with the probe altered to stand one up, it and two neighbours fail. CORRECTED by 0127: this commitment originally also claimed _store_summary read an existing store without writing to it, and that was false -- SqliteStore._connect runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL on every open, so the probe rewrote any store not already in WAL mode. The no-store branch was always clean; the has-store branch was not. See 0127 for the measurement and the read-only fix.
decisions.why: This is the cold-clone trap the agent guide already records, one level in: a command that succeeds by silently creating what it was asked to look for turns 'nothing was ever set up' into 'something just broke', and the wrong conclusion is the easier one to reach. The same instinct that keeps the boot from rebuilding the decision store keeps it from conjuring a Nestor.
